mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's RECENT_5 shots-for (9.8) is materially below its ALL_PRIOR shots-for (12.01) AND Team A's RECENT_5 shots-against (16.4) is materially above its ALL_PRIOR shots-against (10.897). Measure goals-for in matches where both conditions hold simultaneously versus matches where neither holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Goals-for rises with shot production and falls when shot production is simultaneously depressed and shots-conceded is simultaneously elevated — the joint deterioration suppresses scoring more than either condition alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has dropped sharply in recent matches while the shots allowed against them has risen sharply; jointly, when a team's own recent shot production falls below its long-run average AND its recent shots-conceded rises above its long-run average simultaneously, its goals-for output in that match is suppressed relative to its long-run goals-for average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint intersection of two distinct observables (shots-for trend AND shots-against trend) both deviating from their long-run baselines in the same match window. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band; it is a two-observable joint condition.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession gap between the two sides (Team B possession-for minus Team A possession-for) exceeds a threshold derived from the historical distribution of possession gaps in this competition. Within those matches, measure the corner-kick differential (Team A corners-for minus Team B corners-for).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner-kick differential for Team A falls (becomes more negative) as the possession gap in favour of Team B widens — the relationship between possession dominance and corner generation is tested jointly across both teams rather than for either team in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession has declined sharply in recent matches (from a long-run average above 51% to a recent average of 42.2%) while Team B maintains a stable high possession profile (55.8% long-run, 55% recent). The joint possession imbalance between the two sides — measured as the gap between Team B's possession-for and Team A's possession-for in the same match — is associated with a shift in corner-kick differential, because Team A's corners-for has also dropped in recent matches (3.0 recent vs 5.95 long-run) while Team B's corners-for is stable.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (possession and corner kicks) measured asymmetrically across both teams simultaneously, and tests a threshold/non-linear relationship between the possession gap and the corner differential. It is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's offsides-for is above its long-run mean AND Team B's offsides-against is above its long-run mean simultaneously. Within those matches, measure the ratio of Team A goals-for to Team A shots-on-target-for versus the same ratio in matches where neither condition holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's goals-per-shot-on-target is suppressed when both Team A's offside rate and Team B's offside-trap rate are jointly elevated, relative to matches where only one or neither condition holds.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides-against (opponents caught offside against Team B) has spiked sharply in recent matches (4.2 recent vs 2.45 long-run), while Team A's offsides-for (Team A caught offside) has also risen recently (2.8 recent vs 1.86 long-run). The joint condition — Team A running more high-line attacking movements (more offsides) into a defence that is also catching more opponents offside — is associated with a suppression of Team A's shots-on-target conversion into goals, because high-offside-trap defences tend to compress the space in which shots-on-target are generated.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable, two-team condition (Team A offsides-for AND Team B offsides-against) tested against a third observable (goals relative to shots-on-target). It cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both Team A's fouls-against (fouls committed against Team A, i.e. by the opponent) and Team B's fouls-for (fouls committed by Team B) are simultaneously above their respective long-run means. Within those matches, measure total second-half cards (cards_2h) for both teams combined versus the competition context baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total second-half cards rise above the sum of each team's individual card-rate baseline when both teams' foul loads are jointly elevated — the joint condition produces a super-additive card outcome relative to either team's individual foul profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half card rate (cards_2h FOR: 1.283, AGAINST: 1.424) and Team B's second-half card rate (FOR: 1.323, AGAINST: 1.312) both sit above the competition second-half card context mean (1.167). The joint foul-load profile — Team A's recent fouls-against (12.6) rising above its long-run mean (11.08) while Team B's recent fouls-for (12.0) also rises above its long-run mean (10.87) — suggests a match where both teams' foul rates are simultaneously elevated. Test whether the joint elevation of both teams' foul rates is associated with a super-additive increase in second-half cards relative to what each team's individual card rate would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This tests a joint two-team, two-observable condition (Team A fouls-against AND Team B fouls-for simultaneously elevated) against a within-match state outcome (second-half cards). It requires both a half-level split and a two-team joint foul condition, which is not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the attacking team (Team B) has a higher goals-for rate in the second half than the first half AND the defending team (Team A) has a higher goals-against rate in the second half than the first half. Measure whether the combined second-half goal rate in such matches exceeds the first-half goal rate by more than either team's individual half-split would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The second-half goal rate for Team B rises relative to the first half when Team B's own second-half attacking uplift and Team A's second-half defensive drop-off are jointly present — the asymmetric half-split combination across both teams produces a larger second-half goal differential than either team's individual half-split alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-against is split asymmetrically across halves (first-half: 0.444, second-half: 0.646 long-run), while Team B's goals-against is split more evenly (first-half: 0.677, second-half: 0.688). Team A concedes more in the second half than the first, while Team B concedes roughly equally across halves. The joint half-by-half goal-scoring profile — Team B's goals-for in the second half (0.812) exceeds its first-half goals-for (0.635), and Team A's second-half goals-against (0.646) exceeds its first-half goals-against (0.444) — creates a testable asymmetric within-match state: whether the combination of Team B's second-half attacking uplift and Team A's second-half defensive vulnerability jointly produces a higher second-half goal rate than the first-half goal rate in this specific matchup configuration.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split conditioned jointly on both teams' asymmetric half-by-half goal profiles simultaneously — an asymmetric cross-team, within-match state condition. It is not reducible to a single team's half-split in isolation.
